summary.text: A 56-year-old woman of Malian origin, living in France for 20 years, had a history of right breast adenocarcinoma treated in 2017 and paraneoplastic dermatomyositis managed with prednisone, intravenous immunoglobulins, cyclophosphamide, mycophenolate mofetil and rituximab. In 2018 she was referred to dermatology with a small tender subcutaneous nodule on the second phalanx of the fourth finger of the right hand, slowly growing for three months; it had appeared 15 months after immunosuppression began.

Examination showed a mobile, firm, tender 5 mm subcutaneous nodule. CT and PET showed no sign of deep infection, and the leukocyte differential, C reactive protein and β-D-glucans were within normal limits. Excision for a suspected synovial cyst found a pus-filled structure. Histology showed an epithelioid granuloma with filamentous and yeast-like structures, bacterial and mycobacterial cultures were negative, and fungal culture with ITS2 sequencing identified M. romeroi.

Six months after the excision a swelling under the scar and a new adjacent nodule appeared, each one centimeter in diameter, and MRI showed subcutaneous lesions without tendon or bone involvement. Biopsy confirmed recurrence. Terbinafine was replaced by posaconazole after two months, the nodules were excised three months later, and posaconazole continued for three months. One year after it stopped, a 4 × 5 mm nodule recurred, with high amphotericin B and itraconazole MICs.

The second recurrence was treated with wide excision with 3 mm margins and voriconazole 200 mg twice daily for six months. Complete clinical and radiologic remission was still observed 18 months after the surgery and 12 months after antifungal therapy stopped.
